profile.address: Elk Grove Village, Cook County, IL
profile.reading:
STACK Infrastructure's CHI01 campus sits in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, part of the greater Chicago metro area and Cook County, one of ten Americas markets for the Denver, Colorado-headquartered developer and operator, which describes its company-wide footprint as roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets. Chicago has long been a major US data center and telecommunications interconnection hub, anchored historically by carrier-hotel buildings downtown and increasingly supplemented by suburban campuses like Elk Grove Village that offer more available land and power capacity than the dense downtown core. CHI01 consists of two buildings, CHI01A at 12 megawatts across 221,000 square feet and CHI01B at 24 megawatts across 202,000 square feet, together totaling 40 megawatts of IT capacity across 423,000 square feet on 14 acres of land. STACK's Chicago market overall comprises two campuses, CHI01 and this building plus a second campus, CHI02, together totaling 80 megawatts across 32 acres, with STACK's marketing describing CHI01 and CHI02 as offering "high-density flexibility." As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed. STACK's published materials do not state a street address, year of completion, or named power utility (ComEd serves the area generally, though this was not confirmed as CHI01's specific provider), and no independent local news coverage of this campus's permitting or incentive agreements could be located this session. These gaps are recorded rather than filled with unverified detail.

STACK has stated a company-wide net-zero greenhouse gas emissions commitment for 2050, organized under five focus areas covering carbon, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land use and biodiversity, with annual public impact reports. Chicago's data center market has historically centered on downtown carrier-hotel buildings that concentrate network interconnection, with suburban campuses like Elk Grove Village increasingly supplementing that core as available downtown power and space have tightened, a market dynamic that applies to the broader Chicago area rather than to CHI01 specifically.

reading.body:
STACK Chicago CHI01 holds 40 MW of IT capacity on 14 acres in Cook County, a part of the operator's two-campus Chicago footprint totaling 80 MW. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, this capacity translates to roughly 1,000 racks; at 8 accelerators per rack, a typical high-performance cluster, this is approximately 8,000 accelerators. This single facility therefore represents material scale for large-model training or inference workloads.

Illinois has published capacity figures for only six facilities statewide, totaling 236 MW. CHI01 ranks seventh by published megawatts in Illinois despite being within the top facilities, a position that reflects how few operators in the state have disclosed their specifications. The state holds 44 mapped data centers overall, suggesting that most Illinois capacity remains unquantified. This campus is thus one of the few disclosed points in a largely opaque regional market.

The facilities mapped in Illinois include clusters in Chicago and other metros, but comparative capacity is not published for most. CHI01's 40 MW makes it material to Illinois compute infrastructure, though the grid constraints and land availability across Cook County and the broader Midwest will determine whether this campus or its sibling can expand further. The operator has not published opening dates, power specifications, or grid interconnection details for this site.
